biomarkers.label: Weight
biomarkers.about: Body weight. Sudden unintended changes are worth mentioning to a doctor.

biomarkers.label: Body mass index
biomarkers.about: Weight relative to height. Ranges differ for some ethnic groups, for example South Asians.

biomarkers.label: Systolic blood pressure
biomarkers.about: The top blood pressure number, measured while the heart pumps.

biomarkers.label: Diastolic blood pressure
biomarkers.about: The bottom blood pressure number, measured between beats.

biomarkers.label: Resting heart rate
biomarkers.about: Heartbeats per minute at rest.

biomarkers.label: Oxygen saturation
biomarkers.about: How much oxygen your blood carries.

biomarkers.label: Body temperature
biomarkers.about: Core body temperature.

biomarkers.label: White blood cells
biomarkers.about: Immune cells. High counts can mean infection or inflammation, low counts can reduce defences.

biomarkers.label: Red blood cells
biomarkers.about: Cells that carry oxygen.

biomarkers.label: Haemoglobin
biomarkers.about: The oxygen-carrying protein in red cells. Low levels mean anaemia.

biomarkers.label: Haematocrit
biomarkers.about: The share of your blood made of red cells.

biomarkers.label: Platelets
biomarkers.about: Cells that help blood clot.

biomarkers.label: Lymphocytes
biomarkers.about: A type of white cell involved in immunity.

biomarkers.label: Neutrophils
biomarkers.about: White cells that fight bacterial infection.

biomarkers.label: Monocytes
biomarkers.about: White cells that clear debris and fight infection.

biomarkers.label: Eosinophils
biomarkers.about: White cells linked to allergy and parasites.

biomarkers.label: Mean cell volume
biomarkers.about: The average size of red cells.

biomarkers.label: Mean cell haemoglobin
biomarkers.about: The average haemoglobin in each red cell.

biomarkers.label: Fasting glucose
biomarkers.about: Blood sugar after at least 8 hours without food. 100 to 125 is the prediabetes range.

biomarkers.label: HbA1c
biomarkers.about: Average blood sugar over about 3 months. 5.7 to 6.4 is prediabetes and 6.5 or more is the diabetes range.

biomarkers.label: Creatinine
biomarkers.about: A waste product the kidneys clear.

biomarkers.label: eGFR
biomarkers.about: An estimate of kidney filtering. Below 60 for 3 months suggests reduced kidney function.

biomarkers.label: Blood urea nitrogen
biomarkers.about: A waste product linked to kidney function and hydration.

biomarkers.label: ALT
biomarkers.about: A liver enzyme that rises when liver cells are stressed.

biomarkers.label: AST
biomarkers.about: An enzyme found in the liver and muscle.

biomarkers.label: Albumin
biomarkers.about: A protein made by the liver.

biomarkers.label: Total bilirubin
biomarkers.about: A pigment cleared by the liver. High levels cause jaundice.

biomarkers.label: GGT
biomarkers.about: A liver enzyme sensitive to alcohol and bile duct problems.

biomarkers.label: Uric acid
biomarkers.about: High levels can cause gout and kidney stones.

biomarkers.label: Total cholesterol
biomarkers.about: All the cholesterol in your blood. Under 200 is desirable.

biomarkers.label: LDL cholesterol
biomarkers.about: The 'bad' cholesterol. Lower is better for the heart; targets depend on your risk.

biomarkers.label: HDL cholesterol
biomarkers.about: The 'good' cholesterol. Higher is better. Women are advised to stay above 50.

biomarkers.label: Triglycerides
biomarkers.about: Blood fats that rise with sugar, alcohol and weight.

biomarkers.label: TSH
biomarkers.about: Thyroid stimulating hormone, the main thyroid screening test.

biomarkers.label: Total T3
biomarkers.about: An active thyroid hormone.

biomarkers.label: Total T4
biomarkers.about: The main thyroid hormone.

biomarkers.label: Vitamin D
biomarkers.about: Needed for bones and immunity. Below 20 is deficient.

biomarkers.label: Vitamin B12
biomarkers.about: Needed for nerves and blood cells.

biomarkers.label: Ferritin
biomarkers.about: A measure of the body's iron stores.

biomarkers.label: CEA
biomarkers.about: A tumour marker. Smoking and some benign conditions also raise it. It cannot diagnose cancer.

biomarkers.label: CA-125
biomarkers.about: A tumour marker used to follow certain ovarian conditions. It has many benign causes.

biomarkers.label: CA 19-9
biomarkers.about: A tumour marker used to follow certain digestive conditions. Many benign conditions raise it.

biomarkers.label: PSA
biomarkers.about: Prostate-specific antigen. It rises with age and benign prostate conditions as well as cancer.

biomarkers.label: AFP
biomarkers.about: A protein used to follow certain liver conditions.

biomarkers.label: C-reactive protein
biomarkers.about: A general marker of inflammation.

biomarkers.label: ESR
biomarkers.about: A general marker of inflammation that rises with age.

note: Typical adult reference ranges. Laboratories differ, so always use the range printed on your own report.
